sentences.text:
1. This is the revision petition preferred by the State ( prosecution agency before Ld. Trial Court)
against the impugned order dated 11.04.2022 passed by the court of Ld. Metropolitan Magistrate (
Mahila Court), Rohini Courts, Delhi in FIR No. 319/2016, under Section 498A/406/34 IPC of P.S Jahangir Puri , titled as 'State V. Lokesh Kumar & Ors', thereby respondent has been discharged for offence under Section 498A/406/34 IPC.
2.

entities.text:
Metropolitan Magistrate (
Mahila Court), Rohini Courts, Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: As per the case of the petitioner/State the complainant in the present matter got married to Lokesh (accused no1 before the Ld. Trial Court) on 06.02.1997.
After the marriage, she was subjected to cruelty for demand of dowry and physical violence for not bringing cash and motorcycle.

2.1 It is argued on behalf of the petitioner/State that the complainant specifically stated that in the month of July 2000, her husband, mother in law and father in law (respondent herein) gave beating to her.

Her movements were restricted by her mother in law and father in law (respondent herein)
by tying her hands, mouth and also locked her inside the room without any food and water.
She further alleged that after the said incident, on the next day accused persons including respondent herein left her at her parental house and demanded cash of Rs.80,000/- from her parents.
The complainant made 100 number call and against her husband and other family members including respondent herein.

The case was accordingly registered upon the said complaint and arguments were heard and finally charges under Section 498A/406 IPC were framed against accused persons i.e husband while respondent herein was discharged vide impugned order dated 11.04.2022.

2.2 It is further argued that all the above-said facts of the case have been ignored by the Ld. Trial Court and State vs Sukhbir Singh on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98695003/
1
it wrongly discharged the respondent herein.

2.3 It is further argued that the Ld. Trial Court failed to take into consideration the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in case titled B.C. Upreti & Anr. V. State & Anr , Crl. Revision No.
316/2011 decided on 16.07.2015 .

entities.text:
B.C. Upreti & Anr. V. State & Anr , Crl. Revision No.
316/2011
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. Per contra, Ld. Counsel for the respondent has argued that there is no legal infirmity in the impugned order of the Ld Trial Court which calls for any interference.
There is no material on record for proceeding against the respondent.

6. Heard the Ld. Addl. PP for the State/Petitioner and Ld. Counsel for the respondent and considered the material placed on record.
7.
The petitioner/State herein has challenged impugned order whereby the respondent herein has been discharged for want of evidence for the offence under Section 498A/406 IPC.

As far as the petitioner/State is concerned ,there is no dispute with respect to the fact that there is no iota of material on record qua the entrustment of Istidhan articles with respondent herein and its misappropriation.

The only contention is qua the applicability of Section 498A IPC for which the reliance has been placed upon the statement of Shri Rakesh Kumar ( brother of complainant Poonam) and Ms. Savitri Devi ( mother of complainant).
8.

As far as the general allegations of taunts being advanced for dowry , there is no doubt to proposition of law that mere general taunts for bringing less dowry does not fall within four corners of law under Section 498A IPC and in this regard, reliance has been placed by the Ld. Trial Court and rightly so in the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in title viz; State of H.P V. Nikku Ram AIR 1996 SC 67.
9.

entities.text: State of H.P V. Nikku Ram AIR 1996 SC 67
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: But the question herein is as to whether the specific allegations of demand of dowry qua motorcycle and Rs.80,000/- in cash levelled by Smt. Savitri Devi and Rakesh Kumar are sufficient or not for proceeding with charge against the respondent herein.
The prime/star witness cited by the prosecution is complainant Poonam with whom all the alleged incidents of cruelty on account of dowry demand occurred.
She had given a written complaint giving details about the allegations against the accused persons including the respondent herein.
In her entire complaint, no specific allegation are there against the respondent except in para-2 and 5.
As far as the allegations in para-2 are concerned, these are general allegations regarding advancing of taunts for bringing less dowry.

But in Para-5 specific instance has been reported which took place in July 2000 when she was thrashed by the accused persons including respondent herein and was confined in a room on that day on account of dowry demand etc .
On the next day, she was dropped at her mother's home with the allegations that only if Rs.80000/- are brought by her, she can be taken back.
Qua the said specific part of the allegations, the impugned order is completely silent and nothing has been discussed with respect to the said allegations against the respondent herein.

State vs Sukhbir Singh on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98695003/
2 10.

It is well settled proposition of law that the stage of framing of charge the allegations levelled by the witnesses have to be taken to be true unless said allegations appear to be incomprehensible or inconsistent to the other material available on record.
To support this view I am guided by the landmark case of Hon'ble SC in Union Of India vs Prafulla Kumar Samal & Anr 1979 AIR 366.

entities.text: Union Of India vs Prafulla Kumar Samal & Anr 1979 AIR 366
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the present case, the said specific allegations of Poonam against the respondent herein cannot be at all termed to be inconsistent with the other allegations levelled other prosecution witnesses namely Savitri Devi and Rakesh Kumar and others.

11. In view of the above-discussed reasons and observations, I am of the considered opinion that there is material irregularity and legal infirmity in the impugned order which as overlooked the allegations against the respondent .
12. Accordingly, the impugned order dated 11.04.2022 is hereby set aside.

The matter is remanded back to the Ld. Trial Court with directions to proceed for framing of charge against the respondent herein for the offence under Section 498A IPC Parties to appear before the Ld. Trial Court on the date fixed.
TCR be sent back with a copy of this order.
Revision file be consigned to Record Room.
Announced in the Open Court (GAGANDEEP SINGH) on 20.01.2023.

Addl. Sessions Judge/ Spl.
Judge (NDPS), North District, Rohini Courts, Delhi.
